paper_a.title: An iterative thresholding algorithm for linear inverse problems with a sparsity constraint

paper_b.title: A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems

metadata.description: FISTA (paper B) extends ISTA / iterative thresholded Landweber (paper A) by inserting a Nesterov-style momentum / extrapolation step, accelerating the function-value rate from O(1/k) to the optimal O(1/k^2). Paper A introduces the basic proximal-gradient iteration for the l^p-penalized linear inverse problem (with weighted sequence-space penalties and Hilbert-space convergence analysis); paper B repackages the same iteration in finite-dimensional composite-convex form, generalizes the smooth-plus-nonsmooth template, adds a backtracking variant, and contributes the accelerated FISTA scheme together with its O(1/k^2) proof. The pair is paradigmatic of EXT: same proximal-gradient skeleton, B is the strict acceleration.

matches.explanation: Both papers open with the same canonical linear inverse problem: recover f (resp. x) from g = Kf + e (resp. b = Ax + w). Paper A states it in Hilbert-space generality with a bounded operator K, paper B in finite dimensions with a matrix A; the underlying object is identical. Type cross (definition vs problem) is justified because A's definition is precisely the problem statement of B.

Tikhonov regularization functional. A uses ||Kf-g||^2 + mu ||f||^2 (closed-form (K*K + mu I)^{-1} K*g); B uses ||Ax-b||^2 + lambda ||Lx||^2. Both nodes mark this as the standard quadratic-penalty baseline, both are flagged origin: external with Tikhonov as citation.

The l1/lp-regularized least-squares problem. A defines Phi_{w,p}(f) = ||Kf-g||^2 + sum_gamma w_gamma |<f,phi_gamma>|^p for 1 <= p <= 2 (and the matching minimization problem ProbP111.1); B specializes to p=1 with F(x) = ||Ax-b||^2 + lambda ||x||_1. B's ProbP112.4 is the p=1 instance of A's general weighted-lp objective in the canonical orthonormal basis with uniform weights w_gamma = lambda. Marked exact because the names and types align under the standard reduction.

Soft-thresholding / shrinkage operator. A's S_mu(x) = (x - mu/2) sign-cases is identical (up to the standard threshold-parameter convention mu/2 vs alpha) to B's T_alpha(x)_i = (|x_i|-alpha)_+ sgn(x_i). Same operator, same role; the factor-of-2 shift is purely a parameter convention.

A's generalized scalar shrinkage S_{w,p} = (F_{w,p})^{-1} (covering all p in [1,2]) and the vector shrinkage S_{w,p}(h) = sum_gamma S_{w_gamma,p}(h_gamma) phi_gamma generalize B's componentwise soft-threshold T_alpha (which is exactly the p=1, uniform-weight case). Matched analogous because B's operator is a strict special case of A's.

The proximal-gradient / iterative shrinkage update. A's iteration operator T f = S_{w,p}(f + K*(g - Kf)) and the iterate formula f^n = S_{w,p}(f^{n-1} + K*(g - K f^{n-1})) is precisely B's proximal map p_L(y) = argmin_x { g(x) + (L/2) ||x - (y - (1/L) grad f(y))||^2 } evaluated at the previous iterate. Setting f(x) = ||Ax-b||^2 (so grad f(x) = 2 A^T (Ax - b)) and g(x) = lambda ||x||_1, the prox reduces to B's EP112.1 x_{k+1} = T_{lambda t}(x_k - 2 t A^T (A x_k - b)). The two formulations are mathematically identical up to the L = 1 normalization implicit in A's ||K|| < 1 assumption.

Algorithm match: A's iterative thresholded Landweber algorithm IS ISTA. Both papers describe the same procedure - apply K*-residual update then componentwise shrinkage - and B's name 'ISTA' (Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm) is the now-standard label for A's algorithm. A's pseudocode 'f^n = S_{w,p}(f^{n-1} + K*(g - K f^{n-1}))' is the constant-stepsize form of B's x_k = p_L(x_{k-1}) once the operator is suitably normalized.

Composite L2 alignment of the ISTA inner steps. A decomposes its algorithm into init (ASP111.1), the loop body of residual + shrinkage (ASP111.2), and a stop/return (ASP111.3); B has init (ASP112.1) and loop (ASP112.2), explicitly noting the l1 form x_k = T_{lambda/L}(x_{k-1} - (1/L) grad f(x_{k-1})). The step-blocks correspond directly; B does not separately atomize the stopping rule.

A explicitly cites the classical Landweber iteration (origin: external, Landweber 1951) as the unpenalized prior algorithm that ISTA specializes/extends. B's text-extracted JSON does not include a separate Landweber node - although the bare Landweber update x_k = x_{k-1} + 2 A^T (b - A x_{k-1}) is implicit when one reads off ISTA at lambda = 0, B does not name it as a distinct cited result. Listed for completeness; an external-vs-paper match would not affect the pair-level relation type per the prompt rules.

Surrogate functional / quadratic upper bound. A's Phi^SUR_{w,p}(f;a) = Phi_{w,p}(f) + ||f-a||^2 - ||K(f-a)||^2 and Proposition 2.1 (its unique minimizer is S_{w,p}(a + K*(g-Ka)) plus the quadratic excess inequality) play the same role as B's Q_L(x,y) = f(y) + <x-y, grad f(y)> + (L/2)||x-y||^2 + g(x), the proximal-map definition p_L(y), and the optimality lemma LP112.2 characterizing p_L(y) via subgradients. Both encode the same 'majorize then minimize' construction whose minimizer is precisely the proximal-gradient step. Matched exact because the two surrogates differ only in normalization (||K||<1 in A absorbs the L into the identity).

A's non-expansivity lemmas for S_{w,p} (Lemma 2.2) and the iteration operator T (Lemma 3.3) are key intermediate results in A's Opial-based weak-convergence argument. B's analysis is function-value-based (uses LP112.3 three-point inequality + telescoping) and does not require non-expansivity of the prox map as a named lemma. Genuine paper-A-only contribution within the alignment scope.

A's whole strong-convergence machinery for ISTA - Opial's fixed-point theorem (TP111.2, cited), the Phi-monotonicity lemma (LP111.4), uniform boundedness (LP111.5), summable step-sizes (LP111.6), asymptotic regularity (LP111.7), the ||Ku^n||->0 estimate (LP111.8), shrinkage-residual identity (LP111.9, 3.15), norm-from-weak-and-decay lemma (LP111.10, 3.16), and the weak-convergence chain (PrP111.2-PrP111.4) - has no analog in B. B does not establish iterate-norm convergence; it instead bounds F(x_k) - F_* via the three-point inequality and Lemma 4.2 telescoping. This whole cluster is paper-A-specific within the pair.

A's strong-convergence proof (PP111.3, Theorem 3.1) has no counterpart in B. B never proves strong convergence of the iterate sequence; its convergence statement is purely about function values. The PSP111.x children are implicit-by-omission per L2 compactness rules.

B's descent lemma for C^{1,1} functions (f(x) <= f(y) + <x-y, grad f(y)> + (L/2)||x-y||^2 for L >= L(f)) is cited as standard (origin: external, Ortega-Rheinboldt / Bertsekas). A does not state this as a named lemma; A's analysis is structured around the surrogate functional Phi^SUR rather than a Lipschitz-gradient descent inequality. Listed for transparency only - it is external-origin in B and outside the pair-level relation per origin-aware filtering.

B's three-point / sufficient-decrease inequality (Lemma 2.3: F(x) - F(p_L(y)) >= (L/2)||p_L(y)-y||^2 + L<y-x, p_L(y)-y>) and its proof are the workhorse of B's function-value analysis for both ISTA and FISTA. A's PrP111.1 quadratic-excess inequality (Phi^SUR(f+h;a) >= Phi^SUR(f;a) + ||h||^2) plays a structurally similar role but is stated in surrogate-functional form rather than the original F. The connection is real but indirect; both papers use 'majorize-minimize then bound the slack quadratic', so flagging this as paper-B-only is the cleanest call.

Structural analog (separate from the surrogate-vs-prox match above): A's Proposition 2.1 quadratic excess inequality and B's Lemma 2.3 three-point inequality both express the basic descent estimate driving the convergence proofs. They are derived from the same convexity-plus-Lipschitz reasoning but stated in different normalizations; calling this analogous (rather than exact) reflects that A's lives on the surrogate Phi^SUR and B's on F directly.

A's proof of Proposition 2.1 (case analysis on Gamma_0 vs Gamma_1 to show the surrogate quadratic excess) and B's proof of Lemma 2.3 (sufficient-decrease + convexity at y and at p_L(y) + optimality from LP112.2) prove the structurally parallel descent inequalities. Different machinery (case analysis vs subgradient calculus) but same target. L1 parent emitted with composite L2 listing per the v2 rule, since B's PSP children correspond to the steps A's PP111.1 sketches in compressed form.
A's proof of non-expansivity of S_{w,p} (case analysis on F'_{w,p} >= 1 for p>1, direct check for p=1) has no counterpart in B since B does not state non-expansivity as a named lemma.

Both are the 'main convergence theorem for ISTA', but with different convergence modes. A's Theorem 3.1 establishes strong (norm) convergence of the iterate sequence f^n to a minimizer of Phi_{w,p} (qualitative, no rate). B's Theorem 3.1 establishes the O(1/k) function-value rate F(x_k) - F_* <= alpha L(f) ||x_0 - x_*||^2 / (2k). Same algorithm, complementary statements: A gives iterate convergence, B gives function-value rate. Analogous (not exact) because the conclusions are different mathematical objects.

A's regularization theorem (Theorem 4.1: under mu(epsilon)->0 and epsilon^2/mu(epsilon)->0, the regularized solution converges to the generalized solution f^dagger) is a noise-stability / regularization-method result outside B's scope. B treats the optimization problem as fixed; it does not analyze the dependence of the minimizer on noise level or regularization parameter. A-only contribution.

A's Section 4 regularization-theory machinery: regularized-solution definition (DP111.12), modulus of continuity / convergence (DP111.13, DP111.14), Besov norm equivalence (DP111.15, external), smoothing-operator-of-order-alpha (DP111.16, external), pointwise shrinkage bound (LP111.11), weak+norm-equality lemma (LP111.12), and the modulus-of-convergence bracket / rate Propositions 4.4-4.6 (PrP111.5, PrP111.6, PrP111.7). B has no Section-4-equivalent; this is a major paper-A contribution beyond what FISTA covers.
Proofs of the regularization theorem and modulus-of-convergence bounds; counterpart of the unmatched theorem/proposition cluster above. PSP children implicit per L2 compactness.

Pseudo-solution / generalized solution (A) and least-squares problem (B). A's pseudo-solution minimizes ||Kf-g||^2 (the LS criterion) and the generalized solution is its minimum-norm representative; B's LS problem hat{x}_LS = argmin ||Ax-b||^2 is the same criterion in finite dimensions. The min-norm refinement in A is the standard Moore-Penrose-pseudoinverse reading of B's LS.

A introduces frames (DP111.6, origin: external Duffin-Schaeffer 1952) to handle redundant decomposition systems beyond ONBs. B works exclusively in finite-dimensional R^n with the standard basis and does not invoke frame theory. External-origin in A; included because frames are conceptually missing from B's setting.

A's triple-bar (lp-sequence) norm |||f|||_{w,p} on the basis coefficients has no separate node in B because B works directly with the standard l1 norm ||x||_1, which is the special case w_gamma = 1, p = 1 of A's |||.|||_{w,p}. Listed as none for completeness; the underlying object is the natural specialization.

Both encode optimality conditions for the prox / penalized minimizer. A's EP111.2 is the coefficient-wise variational equation 0 in <K*Kf - K*g, phi_gamma> + (w_gamma p / 2) |<f,phi_gamma>|^{p-1} sign(<f,phi_gamma>); B's LP112.2 says z = p_L(y) iff there exists gamma(y) in partial g(z) with grad f(y) + L(z-y) + gamma(y) = 0. Both are first-order optimality conditions for the (regularized/proximal) minimizer; B's is stated abstractly via subgradients, A's instantiates the subgradient of the lp-penalty in coordinates. Analogous, not exact, because of the different formalisms.

A's diagonal-operator generalization (replacing I by D >= K*K + eta I) is a remark about preconditioning the iteration; B does not discuss preconditioning. Remark per compactness rules need not be listed, but kept here as low-confidence none for transparency.

Critical EXT-relation match: A's iterative thresholded Landweber (= ISTA) and B's FISTA are the same algorithm family with FISTA adding a momentum / Nesterov extrapolation step y_{k+1} = x_k + ((t_k-1)/t_{k+1})(x_k - x_{k-1}). FISTA is exactly A's ISTA evaluated at the extrapolated point y_k instead of x_{k-1}. Marked analogous (rather than exact) to flag the inserted acceleration; the per-iteration cost is the same and the objective is identical.

B's backtracking variants of ISTA (AP112.2) and FISTA (AP112.4), with adaptive stepsize 1/L_k chosen via line search, are paper-B-original. A assumes ||K|| < 1 (i.e., L = 1 implicit) and never introduces a backtracking line search; the constant-stepsize is enforced by the operator-norm rescaling. Genuine B-side extension.

Note: AP112.3 (FISTA constant stepsize) IS already linked above as analogous to A's AP111.1. This 'none' entry is NOT a duplicate - it records that FISTA-as-distinct-algorithm (with the t_k recursion and y_{k+1} extrapolation that produce the O(1/k^2) acceleration) has no algorithm-level counterpart on the A side; only the underlying ISTA template does. This is the core EXT signal.

B's O(1/k^2) convergence theorem for FISTA is the central new contribution and has no counterpart in A. A's analysis cannot achieve this rate; A only obtains qualitative (norm) convergence with no rate. This is the hallmark EXT result.

FISTA's analytical machinery: the recursive relation lemma LP112.4 (encoding momentum bookkeeping in (t_k, u_k) sequences), telescoping lemma LP112.5, lower bound t_k >= (k+1)/2 (LP112.6), and the proofs PP112.3 / PP112.4 are all paper-B-original tools that have no counterpart in A's strong-convergence analysis. PSP children implicit per L2 compactness.

B's general composite convex template (P) min { F(x) = f(x) + g(x) } with f smooth + g possibly nonsmooth, plus its standing assumptions, abstracts the framework beyond linear inverse problems. A always works with f(x) = ||Kf - g||^2 + (Hilbert) and a sequence-space lp penalty; the smooth-plus-nonsmooth framing is paper-B's generalization. Important EXT signal in the framing direction (broadens applicability beyond inverse problems).

A's pure-denoising example (K = I, p = 1, recovering Donoho-Johnstone soft-threshold denoising) and B's example showing the l1 LS problem fits framework (P) with f = ||Ax-b||^2, g = ||x||_1, L(f) = 2 lambda_max(A^T A) both function as 'this is the canonical instance' examples but for different aspects: A illustrates a degenerate special case (K = I), B illustrates the framework's coverage of l1-LS. Weak example match.

Numerical-experiment examples. A's 256x256 deconvolution of an ellipse image with Poisson noise (p = 1, 2, with positivity constraint) and B's cameraman / regularization-toolbox deblurring runs (where FISTA is shown to outperform ISTA and MTWIST in iterations to reach a target accuracy) play the same illustrative role: both are 2D image-restoration deblurring case studies validating the proposed iterative scheme. Analogous because the test images and metrics differ; the genre is the same.

A's thresholded SVD example (closed-form minimizer for compact K with SVD) is a structural illustration tied to A's spectral analysis. B has no SVD-style closed-form example. Example-type, weak signal.

Both papers note the convex-set / constrained extension: A says replace S_{w,p} by P_C S_{w,p} for closed convex C; B says all results extend to convex constraints, requiring p_L to remain easy to compute (e.g., nonneg orthant). Same observation in both papers.

A's per-iteration complexity remark (O(N^2) general, O(N) sparse, O(N log N) FFT-implementable). B does not have an analogous complexity-per-iteration remark of this granularity; the closest is RP112.4 (iteration complexity for epsilon-accuracy).
A's asymmetric-penalty extension (replacing w_gamma|f_gamma|^p with w^+_gamma [f_gamma]_+^p + w^-_gamma [f_gamma]_-^p) has no counterpart in B.
A's complex-valued extension (extending S_{w,p} to complex coefficients via S(re^{i theta}) = S(r) e^{i theta}) has no counterpart in B (which is real-valued throughout).

B's monotonicity remark (F(x_k) <= Q_{L_k}(x_k, x_{k-1}) <= F(x_{k-1})) is the discrete analog of A's LP111.4 (monotone decrease of Phi_{w,p}(f^n)) but stated as a remark for ISTA only. Already covered by the LP111.4-vs-(none) cluster above in spirit; recording B-side none for compactness.
B's bounds on L_k (alpha L(f) and beta L(f)) for backtracking. A has no L_k since stepsize is fixed via ||K|| < 1 normalization.

B's iteration-complexity remark (ISTA needs O(1/epsilon) iterations, FISTA needs O(1/sqrt(epsilon)), a strict improvement) is the explicit headline of the EXT relation. No counterpart in A since A has no rate.
